_about: Curated corrections and additions to the people/places/events graph (Theographic Bible Metadata), to TIPNR name relationships, and to ACAI annotations attached to the wrong entity ('acai': 'to' is the value ACAI gives the entity named in 'source', checked at build). The build (scripts/import_theographic.py, scripts/build_database.py) applies them, and scripts/repair_theographic_graph.py and scripts/repair_acai_corrections.py bring an existing database into line. Each correction names the source value it replaces ('from'); if the source changes, the build stops so the correction can be reviewed. Event years are astronomical (-585 is 586 BC); people's years count BC directly (-1758 is 1758 BC).

event_predecessors.reason: Jesus was circumcised on the eighth day (Luke 2:21), not after Herod's massacre of boys up to two years old (Matt 2:16).
The presentation came at the end of the forty days of purification (Luke 2:22; Lev 12:2-4), before the flight to Egypt.
The magi came later than the birth, after the presentation (Matt 2:1, 11, 16: 'a house', boys 'two years old and under').
The family returned from Egypt after Herod died (Matt 2:19-21), so after the massacre, not after the circumcision.
The family settled in Nazareth on returning from Egypt (Matt 2:19-23; Luke 2:39).

David is not a name of the patriarch Judah. At 2 Chr 25:28 the Hebrew has 'the city of Judah' and the ESV 'the city of David'; TIPNR lists that rendering under Judah, and ACAI took it for an alternate label.

Zedekiah was Jehoiakim's brother (1 Chr 3:15), not another name for him. At Jer 27:1 the Hebrew has 'Jehoiakim' and the ESV 'Zedekiah' (as 27:3, 12); TIPNR lists that rendering under Jehoiakim, and ACAI took it for an alternate label.

The John of Acts 4:6 was of the high-priestly family, on the council that tried Peter and John (Acts 4:5-7), not a disciple. (His two attributed speeches, Acts 4:7 and 4:16-17, are the council's, which ACAI attributes to each named member, Alexander and Caiaphas too; they stay.)
Peter and Andrew's father is named only as their father (Matt 16:17; John 1:42; 21:15-17); nothing makes him a disciple.
ACAI's second entity for Peter's father (Matt 16:17), as person:John.4.
His daughter Rizpah's roles (person:Rizpah: Member of the Royal Family, Concubine). Aiah is named only as Rizpah's father (2 Sam 3:7; 21:8-11).

ACAI's two main Gilgals carry each other's text, like the Ramahs. This is TIPNR's Gilgal@Deu.11.30, the Jericho Gilgal of Josh 4-5 and 1 Sam 11-15 (38 references), labelled from its first reference, Deut 11:30 ('near the oaks of Moreh'). place:Gilgal.3 has this town's label.

acai.reason: As its name: the Jericho Gilgal (Josh 4:19-20; 5:9-10).
